title: The Tools
logline: A fisherman's nets, mended and re-mended for thirty years, pass to his son, whose hands are shaped by the same work before he has fully learned it.

object.note: Object 8 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject. Object 7, from The Body, may also sit near hands shaped by work that is being passed on.

thread_in.thread: Death kept close each morning opens onto what continues after it: a fisherman's nets, mended for decades, passing to his son.

thread_out.thread: If nothing passes across and yet everything continues, something must connect it all: from nets passed hand to hand to a tank gate opening, the first link in a chain that ends in a bowl of rice.

lesson.in_simple_terms: The texts say that when a life ends nothing of it crosses into the next, yet what begins is not a stranger: it arises only because of what came before. Worn tools in new hands give a small, everyday picture of that kind of continuity.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: ජීවිතයක් අවසන් වූ විට එයින් කිසිවක් ඊළඟ ජීවිතයට නොයන නමුත්, ඇරඹෙන අලුත් ජීවිතය පෙර තිබූ දෙයේ ඵලයක් ලෙස එම ප්‍රවාහයටම අයත් වන බැවින් එය ආගන්තුකයෙක් නොවන බව ග්‍රන්ථ කියයි.
lesson.the_teaching: The Abhidhamma teaches that the stream of mind runs unbroken from existence to existence, and that when the death-consciousness ends a life, a rebirth-linking consciousness arises at once, with no interval, as the result of the action that was ready to ripen. Both sources insist that nothing mental or physical from the former life passes into the next: the new consciousness did not travel there, it arises there fresh. What links the two is cause and result within one stream, not a traveller.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: The camera stays on the nets and the boat: knots tied one man's way, repairs in his habits, a grip worn into the wood, now in a son's hands before he has fully learned the work. Stories told while working bring the father into the day without anyone saying so, and the viewer is left with an ordinary picture of something continuing without anyone crossing over.

key_terms.en: death consciousness, the last mind of a life
the continuum or stream of mind

lesson.caution: The son is not the father come back, and the tools are not the father living on; in the texts, what continues is a causal stream of mind, not a legacy, a memory or a soul.
lesson.builds_on: The last film kept death close each morning; this one asks what continues after it, and adds that what follows a life is new and yet not a stranger.
